claims.title: Job messages may be intercepted between the web tier and message queue
claims.description: If `unknown:flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job:encryption_in_transit` resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker able to observe the boundary-crossing `flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job` can intercept its business-critical job messages as `process:web-application` enqueues them into `store:message-queue`. The disclosure can reveal work payloads and identifiers that the backend worker subsequently consumes.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses from `boundary:web-tier` to `boundary:backend-tier` and its transport encryption is unstated, although the attacker must obtain an observation position. Impact is medium because the flow carries `business-critical-data` job messages into `store:message-queue`, while their detailed classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the queue connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with service authentication or mTLS on `flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job`, including verification of the queue endpoint.

claims.title: Queue job payloads may be readable on the worker-to-queue connection
claims.description: If `unknown:flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job:encryption_in_transit` resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker with a foothold on the backend path can intercept business-critical job messages as `process:background-worker-process` reads them from `store:message-queue`. Captured jobs expose the inputs that drive downstream worker processing.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because encryption on this internal backend-tier flow is unstated and exploitation requires a backend network observation position. Impact is medium because the flow carries `business-critical-data` job messages from `store:message-queue`.

mitigations.summary: Protect worker queue reads with encrypted transport
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job` to TLS or mTLS and validate both peers.

claims.title: Application and log records may be intercepted on the worker database connection
claims.description: If `unknown:flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records:encryption_in_transit` resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker observing the backend path can intercept application records and log records exchanged between `process:background-worker-process` and `store:database`. The captured records can reveal operational data and log content that may help target the worker or database further.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the encryption state of this internal backend-tier connection is unknown and an attacker needs network-path access. Impact is medium because `store:database` contains application and log records and is tagged `business-critical-data`, although its classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt database client traffic
mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`, validate the database certificate, and use mTLS where supported.

claims.title: Queue credentials may be intercepted while the web application reads configuration
claims.description: If `unknown:flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration:encryption_in_transit` resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker observing the configuration-read path can intercept the message-queue credentials returned by `store:web-application-config` to `process:web-application`. Those credentials can then enable access to the queue beyond the observation point, subject to the queue's separately unstated authentication controls.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the config-read transport protection is unknown and an attacker must observe a web-tier path. Impact is high because `store:web-application-config` holds `credentials` and `secrets`, specifically the queue credentials identified by the credential-custody assertion.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt configuration retrieval
mitigations.detail: Require mutually authenticated TLS between `process:web-application` and `store:web-application-config` so configuration values and queue credentials are confidential in transit.

mitigations.summary: Use short-lived queue access
mitigations.detail: Replace standing queue credentials with narrowly scoped, short-lived workload credentials so an intercepted value has limited reuse value.

claims.title: Database credentials may be intercepted while the worker reads configuration
claims.description: If `unknown:flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration:encryption_in_transit` resolves to no effective transport encryption, an attacker observing the backend configuration path can intercept database credentials returned by `store:worker-config` to `process:background-worker-process`. The stolen credential can enable subsequent database access according to its unstated grant scope.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because encryption is unstated on an internal backend-tier configuration flow and the attacker needs a network observation position. Impact is high because `store:worker-config` contains `credentials` and `secrets`, including the database credentials identified by the credential-custody assertion.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt worker configuration retrieval
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with peer verification or mTLS for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration`.

mitigations.summary: Limit database credential lifetime and scope
mitigations.detail: Issue short-lived, workload-bound database credentials with only the database permissions the worker requires.

claims.title: A message-queue storage copy may disclose queued job data
claims.description: `store:message-queue` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that attribute resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains an operational copy of the queue storage can read queued business-critical job messages without using the normal worker read path. This is conditional on the at-rest control being absent or ineffective; it does not assert that the queue is currently unencrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the queue's at-rest encryption is unstated and a copied storage artifact bypasses application authentication, though obtaining that artifact remains necessary. Impact is medium because `store:message-queue` holds `business-critical-data` job messages, while its classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt queue persistence and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for `store:message-queue`, including durable message storage, backups, snapshots, and replicas, with managed keys and restricted export access.

claims.title: A database storage copy may disclose application and log records
claims.description: `store:database` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that attribute resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a database volume, snapshot, backup, or other operational copy can read the application and log records directly, bypassing `process:background-worker-process` and its database connection. This conditional threat concerns storage-layer copies, not normal authorized database queries.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because encryption at rest for `store:database` is unknown and a storage copy may be obtained outside the application path. Impact is medium because the database contains application and log records and is tagged `business-critical-data`, although the model does not state its classification.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt database files and copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for `store:database` using managed keys, explicitly covering backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media.

mitigations.summary: Protect database copy operations
mitigations.detail: Restrict snapshot, backup, restore, and export permissions to dedicated principals and audit their use.

claims.title: A copied web-application configuration store may reveal queue credentials
claims.description: `store:web-application-config` holds queue credentials and secrets, while `unknown:store:web-application-config:encryption_at_rest` leaves its storage protection unverified. If the store is not effectively encrypted at rest, an attacker obtaining a volume, snapshot, backup, or configuration export can recover the queue credentials without interacting with `process:web-application`. The recovered credential can be used to reach `store:message-queue` according to that queue's separately unstated authentication controls.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because at-rest encryption for `store:web-application-config` is unstated and storage-layer copies can bypass the application. Impact is high because the store is tagged `credentials` and `secrets` and is identified as custody for the queue credential.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt configuration storage and all copies
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce managed-key encryption at rest for `store:web-application-config`, including backups and exports, and restrict access to the corresponding keys.

mitigations.summary: Remove standing queue secrets from configuration
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated secret store and short-lived workload-issued queue credentials rather than long-lived credentials stored with application configuration.

claims.title: A copied worker configuration store may reveal database credentials
claims.description: `store:worker-config` holds database credentials and secrets, while `unknown:store:worker-config:encryption_at_rest` leaves storage protection unverified. If the store is not effectively encrypted at rest, an attacker obtaining its volume, backup, snapshot, or export can recover the database credentials without using `process:background-worker-process`. The recovered credential can enable follow-on access to `store:database` according to its unstated grant scope.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:worker-config` has unverified encryption at rest and a storage copy can bypass normal configuration access. Impact is high because the store holds `credentials` and `secrets`, including the database credential identified by the credential-custody assertion.

mitigations.summary: Protect worker configuration at rest
mitigations.detail: Require managed-key encryption for `store:worker-config` and every backup, snapshot, replica, and export, with separate and audited key-use permissions.

mitigations.summary: Use short-lived database authentication
mitigations.detail: Move database access to short-lived, workload-bound credentials from a dedicated secret mechanism and rotate any existing static credential.

claims.title: Weak or absent queue read authentication could expose job messages
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads from `store:message-queue` through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job`, but that flow's `authentication` is unknown. If the unknown resolves to absent, weak, or overly broad queue read authorization, an attacker who reaches the queue can read business-critical jobs as though they were the worker. The messages may expose workload data before the worker consumes it.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because queue-reader authentication is unstated, so no verified control limits a party that can reach the backend service. Impact is medium because `store:message-queue` and its read-write flow carry `business-critical-data` job messages.

mitigations.summary: Enforce queue-specific reader authorization
mitigations.detail: Require authenticated, distinct worker identities on `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job` and grant each identity only the required queue consume permission.

claims.title: Weak or absent database read authentication could expose records
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads `store:database` through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`, but the flow's `authentication` is unknown. If that unknown resolves to absent, weak, or over-broad authentication and authorization, an attacker able to reach the database can read application and log records without the intended worker identity. The disclosure can provide operational information useful for further attacks against the backend.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because database authentication is unstated, leaving no verified restriction on a party that reaches the database. Impact is medium because `store:database` contains application and log records and is tagged `business-critical-data`, though its classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Require least-privilege database authentication
mitigations.detail: Require a distinct authenticated worker principal on `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`, deny unauthenticated access, and restrict read grants to required tables and columns.

claims.title: Weak configuration-store authentication could disclose queue credentials
claims.description: `process:web-application` reads queue credentials from `store:web-application-config` through `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration`, whose `authentication` is unknown. If the unknown resolves to absent, weak, or overly broad read authorization, an attacker who can reach the configuration store can recover the queue credential. That credential can then be presented to `store:message-queue`, subject to its separately unstated access controls.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because authentication for the configuration read path is unknown, so a reachable store has no verified reader restriction. Impact is high because `store:web-application-config` holds `credentials` and `secrets`, specifically the queue credential.

mitigations.summary: Restrict configuration reads to the web workload
mitigations.detail: Require strong workload authentication and deny-by-default, store-level read authorization on `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration`.

mitigations.summary: Separate and rotate queue credentials
mitigations.detail: Store queue access material in a dedicated secret service, issue short-lived credentials where possible, and rotate any credential exposed by an unauthorized configuration read.

claims.title: Weak configuration-store authentication could disclose database credentials
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads database credentials from `store:worker-config` through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration`, whose `authentication` is unknown. If the unknown resolves to absent, weak, or overly broad read authorization, an attacker who reaches the configuration store can recover the database credential. That disclosure enables follow-on attempts to read `store:database` within the credential's unstated permissions.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the worker configuration read path has unstated authentication, leaving its actual reader restriction unverified. Impact is high because `store:worker-config` holds `credentials` and `secrets`, including the database credential.

mitigations.summary: Authorize only the worker to read worker configuration
mitigations.detail: Enforce workload-bound authentication and deny-by-default reader authorization on `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration`.

mitigations.summary: Replace stored database passwords with workload identity
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived database credentials issued to the worker and rotate any existing database credential that may have been read from configuration.
